subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which textile designer is famous for nature-inspired patterns of the Arts and Crafts movement?
questions.explain: William Morris designed richly patterned, nature-based textiles and wallpapers in the Arts and Crafts style.

questions.q: What is a graphite pencil graded 'H' compared with one graded 'B'?
questions.explain: The 'H' scale denotes harder, paler pencils, while 'B' grades are softer and darker.

questions.q: What is 'visual' (or implied) texture?
options: The appearance of texture created on a flat surface
Texture you can physically feel on the surface
questions.explain: Visual texture is the illusion of texture on a flat surface, whereas actual texture can be touched.

questions.q: Quilting involves...
options: Stitching layers of fabric together, often with wadding between them
questions.explain: Quilting sews together layers of cloth, usually with a padded wadding sandwiched between them.

questions.q: A 'slab' building technique in ceramics uses...
options: Flat sheets of clay joined together
Liquid clay poured into a mould
questions.explain: Slab building cuts and joins flat sheets of clay to make boxes and angular forms.

questions.q: In 3D design, a 'maquette' or model is made to...
options: Test and plan ideas before making the final piece
questions.explain: A model or maquette lets a designer test scale, form and ideas before committing to the final work.

questions.q: What is tie-dye?
options: Binding fabric tightly before dyeing so bound areas resist the dye
questions.explain: In tie-dye, fabric is tied or bound so the bound parts resist the dye, creating patterns.

questions.q: Which artist created the famous ceiling of the Sistine Chapel during the Renaissance?
questions.explain: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling, a masterpiece of the Italian Renaissance.

questions.q: Which genre focuses on capturing real events and everyday life truthfully?
questions.explain: Documentary photography records real events, people and life as honestly as possible.

questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: In the exact centre of the image
Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
Around the edges of the frame
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

questions.q: Considering the 'cultural context' of an artwork means thinking about...
options: Just the size of the canvas
The time, place and society in which it was made
questions.explain: Cultural context considers the historical period, place and society that shaped the artwork.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a sketchbook in GCSE Art?
options: To record ideas and show development of work
questions.explain: A sketchbook records observations, experiments and the development of ideas towards a final piece.

questions.q: Which photographer is famous for dramatic black-and-white landscapes of the American West, such as Yosemite?
questions.explain: Ansel Adams is renowned for his sharp, high-contrast black-and-white landscape photographs.

questions.q: A graphic 'grid' is used to...
options: Organise and align text and images consistently
questions.explain: A grid provides an underlying structure that keeps elements aligned and the layout consistent.

questions.q: 'Architecture' is a branch of design concerned with...
questions.explain: Architecture is the design of buildings and the spaces people use.

questions.q: Which artist is most associated with Pop Art and images of soup cans?
questions.explain: Andy Warhol was a leading Pop Art figure, famous for his Campbell's soup can images.

questions.q: 'Smocking' is a technique that...
options: Gathers fabric with stitches to create decorative texture and stretch
questions.explain: Smocking gathers and stitches fabric to make a flexible, decoratively textured surface.

questions.q: In a landscape, objects placed at the bottom of the picture usually appear to be in the...
questions.explain: Objects lower in the picture plane normally read as nearer to the viewer, in the foreground.

questions.q: A 'relief' sculpture is one where...
options: Forms project from a flat background
questions.explain: In relief, the design is raised from (or sunk into) a flat background rather than standing free.

questions.q: Why is knowing the 'target audience' important in a design?
options: It is only needed for sculpture
It shapes style, tone and content to suit who the design is for
It decides the price of paint
It has no effect on the design
questions.explain: Understanding the target audience guides the style, language and imagery so the design appeals to them.

questions.q: Block printing on fabric works by...
options: Pressing an inked carved block onto the cloth
questions.explain: Block printing presses a raised, inked carved block onto fabric to repeat a motif.

questions.q: Impressionism is best known for...
options: Capturing fleeting light and everyday scenes with loose brushwork
questions.explain: Impressionists used loose, visible brushstrokes to capture changing light and ordinary moments.
